BETA Close X Barratt Redrow plc has announced the purchase of 1,125,000 ordinary shares on March 11, 2026, as part of its £50 million share repurchase program. The shares were acquired from UBS AG London Branch on the London Stock Exchange at a volume-weighted average price of 303.7000 pence per share, with the highest price paid being 304.3000 pence and the lowest at 303.3000 pence. Following these transactions, Barratt Redrow holds no shares in treasury, and its total issued ordinary shares stand at 1,419,151,582, with the total number of voting rights remaining the same. Disclaimer* Barratt Redrow PLC 16 March 2026 16 March 2026 Barratt Redrow plc Transactions in own shares Barratt Redrow plc, ISIN: GB0000811801 (the ""Company"", "Barratt Redrow") announces that during the period from 9 March 2026 to 13th March 2026 (the "Disclosure Period") it has purchased for cancellation the following number of ordinary shares of 10 pence each from UBS AG London Branch ("UBS") as part of its £50 million share repurchase programme announced on 5 January 2026 (the "Programme"). All shares were purchased from UBS as an "on exchange" transaction subject to the rules of the London Stock Exchange ("LSE"). Date of Purchase within Disclosure Period Aggregated volume (shares) Highest price paid per share (pence) Lowest price paid per share (pence) Volume weighted average price (pence) Trading venue 09 March 2026 225,000 307.2000 299.6000 304.3777 LSE 10 March 2026 225,000 314.9000 304.1000 309.1032 LSE 11 March 2026 225,000 304.9000 300.2000 302.5672 LSE 12 March 2026 225,000 298.6000 286.7000 294.9973 LSE 13 March 2026 225,000 291.8000 280.5000 286.5263 LSE To date, Barratt Redrow has purchased 7,475,000 ordinary shares in aggregate for cancellation from UBS in accordance with the Programme. Following the above purchases and cancellation of the ordinary shares, the Company holds no ordinary shares in treasury and has 1,419,151,582 ordinary shares in issue. The total number of voting rights in the Company is therefore 1,419,151,582.
